title: Radians
examples: How do I change degrees to radians?
What is the formula for the area of a sector?
Can you show an example of finding arc length?

explain.say: Today we will learn about radians for angles. Radians are another way to measure angles. They are very useful in trigonometry calculations.
To convert degrees to radians, you multiply by pi over one hundred eighty. This gives you the equivalent angle in radians.

items: Degrees to Radians: Multiply by pi/180

explain.say: For example, ninety degrees is equal to pi divided by two radians. Remember that pi is approximately three point one four one.
Next, let us look at arc length when using radians. The formula for arc length is radius times the angle in radians. It is very straightforward.
If a circle has a radius of five and the angle is two radians, the arc length is ten. You just multiply five by two.

faq.q: What is the relationship between a full circle in degrees and radians?
faq.a: A full circle is always thirty-six hundred and degrees. In radians, a full circle is equal to two pi radians.
asks: How many radians are in a full circle?
What is the radian measure of 360 degrees?

faq.q: Do I need to convert to radians before finding the arc length?
faq.a: Yes, you must use the angle in radians for the arc length formula. Using degrees will give you the wrong answer.
asks: Must the angle be in radians for arc length?
What unit must the angle be in for s = rθ?

faq.q: How do I convert radians back to degrees?
faq.a: To go from radians back to degrees, you multiply the radian measure by one hundred eighty over pi. This reverses the process.
asks: What is the formula for radians to degrees?
If I have radians, how do I find degrees?

faq.q: Is the formula for sector area different if I use radians?
faq.a: Yes, the formula for sector area is one half times radius squared times the angle in radians. This is different from using degrees.
asks: What is the area formula using radians?
Does the angle unit matter for sector area?

faq.q: What is the difference between arc length and sector area?
faq.a: Arc length is just a length along the curve, like a piece of string. Sector area is the amount of flat space inside the curved slice.
asks: Is arc length a distance or an area?
What measures the space inside a sector?

facts: A full circle measures thirty-six hundred degrees.
Two pi radians equals one full circle.
Arc length is calculated by multiplying the radius by the angle in radians.
Sector area is calculated using one half times radius squared times the angle in radians.

quiz.why: Ninety degrees is exactly one quarter of a full circle, and pi divided by two is one quarter of two pi.

wrong.0: This incorrectly places ninety in the denominator instead of the numerator.
wrong.2: This is the conversion factor, not the result for ninety degrees.
wrong.3: This incorrectly divides the degrees by pi instead of multiplying by pi over one hundred eighty.

quiz.say: Find the arc length if the radius is seven and the angle is pi over three radians.

options.show: seven plus pi divided by three
options.say: seven plus pi divided by three

options.show: seven squared times pi divided by three
options.say: seven squared times pi divided by three

options.show: seven times three divided by pi
options.say: seven times three divided by pi

quiz.why: The formula is radius times angle, so seven times pi divided by three gives the correct length.

wrong.1: You should multiply the radius by the angle, not add them together.
wrong.2: Squaring the radius is only used for area calculations, not for arc length.
wrong.3: This incorrectly rearranges the numbers and uses pi in the denominator.

quiz.say: Calculate the area of a sector with a radius of ten and an angle of two radians.

options.show: one half times ten plus two
options.say: one half times ten plus two

quiz.why: The formula is one half times radius squared times angle, so one half times one hundred times two is one hundred.

wrong.1: This calculates the arc length, not the area of the sector.
wrong.2: This only uses the radius squared and ignores the angle measurement.
wrong.3: This incorrectly adds the angle instead of multiplying it by the radius squared.
